043/**
044 * Provides String based properties like {@link System#getProperty(String)} for default
045 * configuration of logging levels and output. Since Rainbow Gum is configuration agnostic
046 * LogProperties is a simple string key and string value interface to allow almost any
047 * configuration implementation. The only required method to implement is
048 * {@link #valueOrNull(String)} and thus LogProperties is a functional like interface but
049 * using {@link LogProperties#builder()} is preferred so that a
050 * {@linkplain #description(String) description} can be added.
051 * <p>
052 * If a custom {@link LogProperties} is not configured the default RainbowGum uses System
053 * properties.
054 * <p>
055 * The built-in properties to configure RainbowGum are modeled after <a href=
056 * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/3.1.0/reference/html/features.html#features.logging">
057 * Spring Boot logging </a>
058 * <p>
059 * LogProperties should generally be accessed with {@link #forKey(String)} (see
060 * {@link LogProperty}) which will allow safe <em>programmatic</em> data conversion of the
061 * flat key values and useful error messages to users if the property cannot be mapped or
062 * is missing. For more <em>declarative</em> injection of properties see
063 * {@link LogConfigurable} which will generate builders that can use LogProperties.
064 * <p>
065 * Rainbow Gum treats {@value #SEP} in the keys as special separator analogous to
066 * JavaScript/JSON and various other configuration systems. Furthermore to work with a
067 * wide set of configuration systems once a property key has a value it is
068 * <strong>RECOMMENDED</strong> that there should not be other property key value with a
069 * key that is a prefix of the previously mentioned key. For example allowing two
070 * properties <code>logging.example=stuff</code>, <code>logging.example.a=A</code> is not
071 * recommended as <code>logging.example</code> is defined as a leaf. The exception to this
072 * rule is keys that end with a logger name, such as levels, for consistency with Spring
073 * Boot. {@link AbstractNested} is one way for a nested format to read them.
074 * <p>
075 * Rainbow Gum out of the the box supports parsing two formats into properties:
076 * {@link Properties} text, and {@link URI#getRawQuery()} percent encoded query
077 * parameters. The two different formats have different behavior for
078 * {@link #listOrNull(String)} and {@link #mapOrNull(String)}. If a custom format of
079 * LogProperties is created those two methods may need to be extended.
080 * <p>
081 * A convention used through out Rainbow Gum is to have the property names as constants as
082 * it makes documentation easier. These constants name are suffixed with
083 * <code>_PROPERTY</code> or <code>_PREFIX</code> the former being a fully qualified key
084 * that maybe parameterized and the latter being a partial key ending with
085 * "<code>.</code>". The fully qualified keys are like leaves on a tree.
086 * <p>
087 * Property keys can be parameterized by using
088 * {@link LogProperties#interpolateKey(String, Map)} and a general pattern is
089 * <code>logging.component.{name}.prop</code> where {@value #NAME} is a parameter. Many
090 * property constants use this to allow multiple configuration of components by name.
091 *
092 * <table class="table">
093 * <caption><strong>Built-in Property Patterns</strong></caption>
094 * <tr>
095 * <th>Property Pattern</th>
096 * <th>Description</th>
097 * </tr>
098 * <tr>
099 * <td>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = LEVEL</td>
100 * <td>Sets the level for the logger. If logger name is missing or is <code>root</code>
101 * then it is considered the root logger. {@link Level#INFO} is the default level for the
102 * root logger.</td>
103 * </tr>
104 * <tr>
105 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} = {@link ChangeMode}</td>
106 * <td>Whether runtime changes are on for the configuration. Default is
107 * {@link ChangeMode#OFF}. When on, the loggers that may change are chosen with
108 * {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX}.</td>
109 * </tr>
110 * <tr>
111 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = boolean |
112 * List&lt;{@link ChangeType}&gt;</td>
113 * <td>What may change at runtime for the logger and its children. By design RainbowGum
114 * does not allow loggers to change levels once initialized. Default is none. Has no
115 * effect unless {@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} is on.</td>
116 * </tr>
117 * <tr>
118 * <td>{@value #ROUTES_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
119 * <td>A comma separated list of routes that should be enabled. If not set
120 * {@value LogRouter.Router#DEFAULT_ROUTER_NAME } is the default.</td>
121 * </tr>
122 * <tr>
123 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
124 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders associated with the route. If not set
125 * {@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} is used.</td>
126 * </tr>
127 * <tr>
128 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_FILTERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
129 * <td>A comma separated list of {@linkplain LogRouter.Router.Filter filters} applied in
130 * order to the route's events. Default is none.</td>
131 * </tr>
132 * <tr>
133 * <td>{@value #FILTER_PREFIX} + <code>propertyName</code></td>
134 * <td>Configures a filter listed in {@value #ROUTE_FILTERS_PROPERTY}, where
135 * <code>filter</code> is the name it is listed with, for example
136 * <code>logging.route.default.filter.throttle.rate</code>.</td>
137 * </tr>
138 * <tr>
139 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY} = <code>URI</code></td>
140 * <td>Looks up a publisher by URI scheme using the {@link LogPublisherRegistry}. The
141 * publisher is then configured by the other properties starting with
142 * {@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX}.</td>
143 * </tr>
144 * <tr>
145 * <td>{@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
146 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
147 * <td>Configures the route's publisher of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
148 * example <code>logging.route.default.publisher.async.bufferSize</code>. The scheme is
149 * the one written in the URI, so <code>async</code> settings apply to whichever publisher
150 * is registered as <code>async</code>.</td>
151 * </tr>
152 * <tr>
153 * <td>{@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
154 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders that should be enabled. If not set
155 * {@value LogAppender#CONSOLE_APPENDER_NAME} is the default.</td>
156 * </tr>
157 * <tr>
158 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
159 * <td>Looks up an output by URI scheme using the {@link LogOutputRegistry}. The output is
160 * then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX}.</td>
161 * </tr>
162 * <tr>
163 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
164 * <td>Looks up an encoder by URI scheme using the {@link LogEncoderRegistry}. The encoder
165 * is then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #ENCODER_PREFIX}.</td>
166 * </tr>
167 * <tr>
168 * <td>{@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
169 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
170 * <td>Configures the appender's output of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
171 * example <code>logging.appender.file.output.file.bufferSize</code>. An output built
172 * without an appender uses its own name in place of the appender's.</td>
173 * </tr>
174 * <tr>
175 * <td>{@value #ENCODER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
176 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
177 * <td>Configures the appender's encoder of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
178 * example <code>logging.appender.console.encoder.json5.keyValues</code>. Each type has
179 * its own keys, so switching an appender's encoder leaves the other type's settings
180 * unread rather than misread. An encoder built without an appender uses its own name in
181 * place of the appender's.</td>
182 * </tr>
183 * <tr>
184 * <td>{@value #FILE_PROPERTY} = URI</td>
185 * <td>A URI or file path to log to a file. This is for Spring Boot compatibility.</td>
186 * </tr>
187 * </table>
188 *
189 * @see LogConfigurable
190 */
191public interface LogProperties {
192
193        /**
194         * properties separator.
195         */
196        static final String SEP = ".";
197
198        /**
199         * Logging properties prefix.
200         */
201        static final String ROOT_PREFIX = "logging" + SEP;
202
203        /**
204         * Controls direct fail-safe bootstrap diagnostics. {@code OFF} (also {@code false})
205         * is the default; {@code ERROR} dumps on build failure, while {@code INFO} also dumps
206         * after successful config builds. {@code ALL} (also {@code true}) additionally prints
207         * a {@link LogReporter} report after {@link RainbowGum#start()} starts the logging
208         * components. Read from system properties before properties providers run, so it
209         * remains available when loading configuration fails. The system property overrides
210         * {@link LogConfig.Builder#debug(LogConfig.DebugModeType)}.
211         * <p>
212         * Property: <code>{@index logging.debug}</code>
213         */
214        static final String DEBUG_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "debug";
215
216        /**
217         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
218         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
219         * <p>
220         * Property: <code>{@index logging.level.{logger}}</code>
221         */
222        static final String LEVEL_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "level";
223
224        /**
225         * Enabled level groups. The value should be a list of group names used on
226         * {@link #GROUP_PROPERTY}. This is to enable <a href=
227         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
228         * Spring Boot like Log Groups </a>. <em>Note that unlike Spring Boot groups are not
229         * enabled unless this property contains the group.</em>
230         * <p>
231         * Property: <code>{@index logging.groups}</code>
232         */
233        static final String GROUPS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "groups";
234
235        /**
236         * Group property with list of logger names. The level of the group is set with
237         * <code>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code> or on the router itself with
238         * <code>{@value #ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code>. The group name can
239         * also be used in place of a logger name with {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and
240         * {@value #CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX}. This is largely compatible with <a href=
241         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
242         * Spring Boot Log Groups </a>.
243         * <p>
244         * Property: <code>{@index logging.group.{name}}</code>
245         * @see LevelResolver#parseLevel(String)
246         */
247        static final String GROUP_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "group.{name}";
248
249        /**
250         * Whether runtime changes are on: see {@link ChangeMode}.
251         * <p>
252         * Property: <code>{@index logging.change.mode}</code>
253         */
254        static final String CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.mode";
255
256        /**
257         * The level threshold of events captured before Rainbow Gum is fully bound. Before
258         * Rainbow Gum is bound events are queued. By default events that are below
259         * <code>INFO</code> are not queued.
260         * <p>
261         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.queue.level}</code>
262         */
263        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_LEVEL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.level";
264
265        /**
266         * The level threshold of queued events reported to standard error before Rainbow Gum
267         * is bound. Defaults to <code>ERROR</code>.
268         * <p>
269         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.queue.error}</code>
270         */
271        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_ERROR_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.error";
272
273        /**
274         * The line separator formatters end lines and stack trace lines with: <code>lf</code>
275         * (default) for <code>\n</code>, <code>crlf</code> for <code>\r\n</code>, or
276         * <code>platform</code> for {@link System#lineSeparator()}. Read once, from system
277         * properties only.
278         * <p>
279         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.lineSeparator}</code>
280         */
281        static final String GLOBAL_LINE_SEPARATOR_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.lineSeparator";
282
283        /**
284         * Whether output uses ANSI escape codes: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode}.
285         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode#AUTO}.
286         * <p>
287         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.ansi.mode}</code>
288         */
289        static final String GLOBAL_ANSI_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.ansi.mode";
290
291        /**
292         * Which kind of lock appenders use: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock}.
293         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock#AUTO}.
294         * <p>
295         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.appender.lock}</code>
296         */
297        static final String GLOBAL_APPENDER_LOCK_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.appender.lock";
298
299        /**
300         * Whether the logging path may use a {@link ThreadLocal}: see
301         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode}. Default is
302         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode#ALLOW}.
303         * <p>
304         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.threadLocal}</code>
305         */
306        static final String GLOBAL_THREAD_LOCAL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.threadLocal";
307
308        /**
309         * Opts every appender/encoder that has not been given an explicit choice into
310         * whatever this release currently believes is the best buffering/locking strategy for
311         * the platform the process is actually running on, instead of the fixed defaults
312         * ({@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}, a
313         * {@link java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder}-based encode) used otherwise. An explicit
314         * choice - programmatic ({@code appenderType(...)}, {@code useGetBytes(...)}) or via
315         * a more specific property ({@link LogAppender#APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY}) - always wins
316         * over this property; it only ever fills in what would otherwise be unset.
317         * <p>
318         * <strong>What "best" resolves to today, and why that is not a contract:</strong>
319         * currently this only has an effect under GraalVM native-image (detected the same way
320         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#AUTO_DETECT} is - see its javadoc), where it sets
321         * the default appender type to {@code AUTO_DETECT} (this benchmark's own measurements
322         * found {@code SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} a real, repeatable win over the
323         * plain-JVM default there) and defaults text encoders to
324         * {@code String.getBytes(Charset)}-based encoding over the default
325         * {@code CharsetEncoder}-based one. On a plain JVM this property currently changes
326         * nothing at all - the measurements that motivated the native-image behavior above
327         * pointed the other way on HotSpot. None of this is a promise: as this project
328         * benchmarks more platforms, JDK versions, and encode strategies, what "optimize"
329         * resolves to on a given platform - including whether it does anything on a plain JVM
330         * at all - can and will change between releases without notice. Pin an explicit
331         * appender type/encoder strategy instead if a deployment needs a specific one to
332         * always be used.
333         * <p>
334         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.optimize}</code>
335         */
336        static final String GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.optimize";
337
338        /**
339         * How the java.util.logging, System.Logger and JBoss Logging message style formats a
340         * message with arguments, named after the implementation that formats the same way:
341         * <ul>
342         * <li><code>jdk</code> (default, alias <code>jboss</code>):
343         * {@link java.text.MessageFormat} is used only when the message has an argument index
344         * such as <code>{0}</code>, so <code>It's done</code> is logged as is. A
345         * {@link Throwable} argument is formatted like any other argument.</li>
346         * <li><code>log4j2</code> (alias <code>logback</code>):
347         * {@link java.text.MessageFormat} is used whenever the message has arguments, so
348         * <code>It's done</code> with an argument is logged as <code>Its done</code>, because
349         * an apostrophe is a quote. A {@link Throwable} that is the last argument is
350         * formatted like any other argument and also logged with its stack trace.</li>
351         * </ul>
352         * <p>
353         * Property: <code>{@index logging.messageformat.style}</code>
354         * @see LogMessageFormatter#ofJUL(LogProperties)
355         */
356        static final String MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "messageformat.style";
357
358        /**
359         * Key values namespace, for properties that configure where an event's key values
360         * come from.
361         */
362        static final String KEY_VALUES_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "keyvalues" + SEP;
363
364        /**
365         * A comma separated list of the key value sources whose contributors add key values
366         * to events, as the lowercase names of
367         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard}, for example
368         * <code>defaults,slf4j</code>. When absent every source is selected, and an empty
369         * value selects none. A logging facade's own context store is always used for events
370         * logged through that facade, whether or not it is selected, and
371         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor#clear()} clears a store that is not
372         * selected according to
373         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard#clearWhenUnselected()}.
374         * <p>
375         * Property: <code>{@index logging.keyvalues.sources}</code>
376         */
377        static final String KEY_VALUES_SOURCES_PROPERTY = KEY_VALUES_PREFIX + "sources";
378
379        /**
380         * Maximum number of alerts {@link LogAlerts} holds in its ring buffer. Read once,
381         * from whatever {@link LogProperties} {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} has already
382         * resolved by the time it constructs {@link LogAlerts} - before any
383         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} runs.
384         * <p>
385         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.capacity}</code>
386         * @see LogAlerts#DEFAULT_CAPACITY
387         */
388        static final String ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.capacity";
389
390        /**
391         * What {@link LogAlerts} does, once on {@link LogLifecycle#start(LogConfig) start},
392         * if it has recorded at least one error alert and still has zero
393         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener}s registered - see
394         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction} for the three choices and
395         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction#DUMP} for the default.
396         * <p>
397         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction}</code>
398         */
399        static final String ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unobservedErrorsAction";
400
401        /**
402         * Alert level at which starting Rainbow Gum fails, like treating compiler warnings as
403         * errors: see {@link LogAlerts.FailLevel}. Unlike
404         * {@value #ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY} it fails whether or not a
405         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener} is registered.
406         * <p>
407         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.fail}</code>
408         */
409        static final String ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.fail";
410
411        /**
412         * Alert level for property keys that were set but not read while starting: see
413         * {@link LogAlerts.UnusedKeyLevel}.
414         * <p>
415         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.unusedKey}</code>
416         */
417        static final String ALERTS_UNUSED_KEY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unusedKey";
418
419        /**
420         * Per logger change properties prefix: see {@link ChangeType}.
421         * <p>
422         * Property: <code>{@index logging.change.logger.{logger}}</code>
423         */
424        static final String CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.logger";
425
426        /**
427         * Per logger caller info properties prefix: see {@link LogEvent.Caller.CallerType}.
428         * Independent of {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and {@link #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY}:
429         * resolved through its own logger-name hierarchy walk, so a value here is never
430         * overridden by a more specific {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} entry or vice versa.
431         * <p>
432         * Property: <code>{@index logging.caller.logger.{logger}}</code>
433         */
434        static final String CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "caller.logger";
435
436        /**
437         * Logging file property for default single file appending. The value is a URI or a
438         * file path, including a Windows path such as <code>C:\logs\app.log</code>.
439         * <p>
440         * Property: <code>{@index logging.file.name}</code>
441         */
442        static final String FILE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "file.name";
443
444        /**
445         * A common key parameter is called name.
446         */
447        static final String NAME = "name";
448
449        /**
450         * For properties keys that are parameterized with {@value #NAME} the name often used
451         * if not specified is: {@value #DEFAULT_NAME}.
452         */
453        static final String DEFAULT_NAME = "default";
454
455        /**
456         * Enabled Logging appenders. The value should be a list of names. This is equivalent
457         * to {@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} with name "default".
458         * <p>
459         * Property: <code>{@index logging.appenders}</code>
460         */
461        static final String APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "appenders";
462
463        /**
464         * Logging appender prefix for configuration.
465         */
466        static final String APPENDER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "appender.{" + NAME + "}.";
467
468        /**
469         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's output, followed by the output's
470         * URI scheme, for example <code>logging.appender.{name}.output.file.</code>. Also
471         * used for an output built without an appender.
472         */
473        static final String OUTPUT_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "output.";
474
475        /**
476         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's encoder, followed by the
477         * encoder's URI scheme, for example
478         * <code>logging.appender.{name}.encoder.json5.</code>. Also used for an encoder built
479         * without an appender.
480         */
481        static final String ENCODER_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "encoder.";
482
483        /**
484         * Output appender property.
485         * <p>
486         * Property: <code>{@index logging.appender.{name}.output.uri}</code>
487         */
488        static final String APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY = OUTPUT_PREFIX + "uri";
489
490        /**
491         * Encoder appender property.
492         * <p>
493         * Property: <code>{@index logging.appender.{name}.encoder.uri}</code>
494         */
495        static final String APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY = ENCODER_PREFIX + "uri";
496
497        /**
498         * Appender flags. A list of flags (usually comma separated).
499         * <p>
500         * Property: <code>{@index logging.appender.{name}.flags}</code>
501         * @see AppenderFlag
502         */
503        static final String APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "flags";
504
505        /**
506         * Appender type (buffer/locking strategy). Unlike {@value #APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY}
507         * this is a single value, not a list.
508         * <p>
509         * Property: <code>{@index logging.appender.{name}.type}</code>
510         * @see LogAppender.AppenderType
511         */
512        static final String APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "type";
513
514        /**
515         * Routes enabled with names comma separated.
516         * <p>
517         * Property: <code>{@index logging.routes}</code>
518         */
519        static final String ROUTES_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "routes";
520
521        /**
522         * Route prefix for configuration.
523         */
524        static final String ROUTE_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "route.{" + NAME + "}.";
525
526        /**
527         * Prefix of the properties configuring a route's publisher, followed by the URI
528         * scheme of {@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY}, for example
529         * <code>logging.route.{name}.publisher.async.</code>. Also used for a publisher built
530         * without a route.
531         */
532        static final String PUBLISHER_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "publisher.";
533
534        /**
535         * Logging publisher URI property.
536         * <p>
537         * Property: <code>{@index logging.route.{name}.publisher.uri}</code>
538         */
539        static final String ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY = PUBLISHER_PREFIX + "uri";
540
541        /**
542         * Appenders associated with a route comma separated.
543         * <p>
544         * Property: <code>{@index logging.route.{name}.appenders}</code>
545         */
546        static final String ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "appenders";
547
548        /**
549         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
550         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
551         * <p>
552         * Property: <code>{@index logging.route.{name}.level.{logger}}</code>
553         */
554        static final String ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "level";
555
556        /**
557         * Route flags.
558         * <p>
559         * Property: <code>{@index logging.route.{name}.flags}</code>
560         */
561        static final String ROUTE_FLAGS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "flags";
562
563        /**
564         * Comma separated names of the {@link LogRouter.Router.Filter filters} applied, in
565         * the order listed, to the route's events. An unknown name fails when the route is
566         * built.
567         * <p>
568         * Property: <code>{@index logging.route.{name}.filters}</code>
569         */
570        static final String ROUTE_FILTERS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "filters";
571
572        /**
573         * Key parameter for the name a {@link LogRouter.Router.Filter filter} is selected
574         * with in {@value #ROUTE_FILTERS_PROPERTY}.
575         */
576        static final String FILTER = "filter";
577
578        /**
579         * Prefix of the properties configuring a route's filter, for example
580         * <code>logging.route.default.filter.throttle.rate</code>.
581         */
582        static final String FILTER_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "filter.{" + FILTER + "}.";

584        /**
585         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String)}.
586         * @param key property name.
587         * @return property value.
588         */
589        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key);
590
591        /**
592         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String, String)} with the exception that the
593         * fallback cannot be null and the return cannot be null.
594         * @param key property name.
595         * @param fallback returned if the value is not found and may not be null.
596         * @return value found or fallback.
597         */
598        default String value(String key, String fallback) {
599                Objects.requireNonNull(fallback);
600                String v = valueOrNull(key);
601                if (v != null) {
602                        return v;
603                }
604                return fallback;
605        }
606
607        /**
608         * Gets a list or null if the key is missing and by default uses
609         * {@link #parseList(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
610         * as a list using {@link LogProperties#parseList(String)} but custom implementations
611         * may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing
612         * configuration system.
613         * <p>
614         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
615         * and percent-encoded (<a href=
616         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
617         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
618         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
619         * logging.appenders=console,file
620         * </code></pre> resolves to <code>["console", "file"]</code>, and: <pre><code>
621         * logging.appenders=one%20two,three%2Cfour
622         * </code></pre> (a space and an escaped comma) resolves to
623         * <code>["one two", "three,four"]</code>. See {@link #parseList(String)} for empty
624         * elements.
625         * @param key property name.
626         * @return list or <code>null</code>.
627         * @apiNote the reason empty list is not returned for missing key is that it creates
628         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
629         */
630        default @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
631                String s = valueOrNull(key);
632                if (s == null) {
633                        return null;
634                }
635                return parseList(s);
636        }
637
638        /**
639         * Gets a map or null if the key is missing and by default uses
640         * {@link #parseMap(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
641         * as map using {@link LogProperties#parseMap(String)} but custom implementations may
642         * rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration
643         * system.
644         * <p>
645         * The returned map must iterate in a stable order, the same every time for the same
646         * configuration, preferably the order its entries were declared.
647         * <p>
648         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
649         * <code>key=value</code> pairs, percent-encoded (<a href=
650         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
651         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
652         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
653         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=environment=prod,region=us-east
654         * </code></pre> resolves to
655         * <code>{"environment": "prod", "region": "us-east"}</code>, and: <pre><code>
656         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=region=us%20east
657         * </code></pre> (a percent-encoded space) resolves to
658         * <code>{"region": "us east"}</code>.
659         * <p>
660         * When that property is not set, the map can instead be given as a list of its keys
661         * in <code>key.keys</code> and each value in <code>key.</code><em>mapKey</em>, which
662         * works with sources that only hold flat values such as system properties or
663         * environment variables, keeps the declared order, and needs no encoding: <pre><code>
664         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.keys=environment,region
665         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.environment=prod
666         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.region=us east
667         * </code></pre> A key listed without a value is an error.
668         * @param key property name.
669         * @return map or <code>null</code>.
670         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if a key listed in <code>key.keys</code> is empty
671         * or has no value.
672         * @apiNote the reason empty map is not returned for missing key is that it creates
673         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
674         */
675        default @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
676                String s = valueOrNull(key);
677                if (s == null) {
678                        return PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
679                }
680                return parseMap(s);
681        }
682
683        /**
684         * Suffix of the property listing a map's keys, see {@link #mapOrNull(String)}.
685         */
686        static final String MAP_KEYS_SUFFIX = "keys";
687
688        /**
689         * Visits this properties with visitor, by default just applying visitor to this and
690         * key directly. A composite/aggregate {@link LogProperties} (one backed by more than
691         * one underlying source) overrides this to recursively visit each of its members in
692         * order, returning the first non-<code>null</code> result - which member actually
693         * produced it is exactly what visitor is handed as its first argument, so a composite
694         * never needs to know anything about what visitor is trying to build (a raw value, a
695         * resolved property, or anything else); it just walks its members and stops at the
696         * first hit.
697         * @param <R> result type.
698         * @param key property key.
699         * @param visitor applied to (the member of this properties that ends up handling the
700         * visit, key); a <code>null</code> return means keep visiting.
701         * @return first non-<code>null</code> result, or <code>null</code> if nothing visited
702         * produced one.
703         */
704        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
705                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
706                return visitor.apply(this, key);
707        }
708
709        /**
710         * Searches up a {@value #SEP} separated path using this properties to check for
711         * values. The first value not missing (not <code>null</code>) will be returned.
712         * @param <T> result type
713         * @param root prefix.
714         * @param key partial key that will have prefix concated on each try of func.
715         * @param func convert function where <code>null</code> return means to keep
716         * searching.
717         * @return closest value or <code>null</code> if no value can be found.
718         * @see #findUpPathOrNull(String, Function)
719         */
720        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
721        default <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findOrNull(String root, String key,
722                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable T> func) {
723                return findUpPathOrNull(key, k -> func.apply(this, concatKey(root, k)));
724        }
725
726        /**
727         * Starts resolving a property under key against this properties - the preferred entry
728         * point for looking up and converting a property, see {@link LogProperty}.
729         * @param key key, must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with
730         * {@value #SEP}.
731         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
732         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
733         * {@link LogProperty#or(String)}).
734         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if key is malformed.
735         */
736        default LogProperty forKey(String key) {
737                return LogProperty.of(this, key);
738        }
739
740        /**
741         * Starts resolving a property under key, with a <code>{name}</code> placeholder in
742         * key interpolated to nameParam, against this properties.
743         * @param key key, containing a <code>{name}</code> placeholder, and once interpolated
744         * must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with {@value #SEP}.
745         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code> in key.
746         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
747         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
748         * {@link LogProperty#or(String, String)}).
749         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the interpolated key is malformed.
750         */
751        default LogProperty forKey(String key, String nameParam) {
752                return LogProperty.of(this, key, nameParam);
753        }
754
755        /**
756         * Describes a key and by default is usually just the key.
757         * @param key key.
758         * @return usually the key.
759         */
760        default String description(String key) {
761                return key;
762        }
763
764        /**
765         * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A higher
766         * number gives higher precedence.
767         * @return zero by default.
768         */
769        default int order() {
770                return 0;

773        /**
774         * Abstract log properties builder.
775         *
776         * @param <T> builder.
777         * @apiNote this abstract class can largely be ignored hence why it is sealed.
778         */
779        public sealed abstract class AbstractBuilder<T> {
780
781                /**
782                 * description
783                 */
784                protected @Nullable String description = null;
785
786                /**
787                 * order
788                 */
789                protected int order = 0;
790
791                /**
792                 * rename key
793                 */
794                protected Function<String, String> renameKey = s -> s;
795
796                /**
797                 * fallbacks
798                 */
799                protected List<LogProperties> fallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
800
801                /**
802                 * Ignored.
803                 */
804                protected AbstractBuilder() {
805                }
806
807                /**
808                 * Add a fallback properties.
809                 * @param properties fallback not null.
810                 * @return this.
811                 */
812                public T with(LogProperties properties) {
813                        this.fallbacks.add(properties);
814                        return self();
815                }
816
817                /**
818                 * For returning this.
819                 * @return this builder.
820                 */
821                protected abstract T self();
822
823                /**
824                 * Description for properties.
825                 * @param description not null.
826                 * @return this.
827                 */
828                public T description(String description) {
829                        this.description = description;
830                        return self();
831                }
832
833                /**
834                 * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A
835                 * higher number gives higher precedence.
836                 * @param order order.
837                 * @return this.
838                 */
839                public T order(int order) {
840                        this.order = order;
841                        return self();
842                }
843
844                /**
845                 * Renames the key before it accesses function.
846                 * @param renameKey rename key function.
847                 * @return this.
848                 */
849                public T renameKey(Function<String, String> renameKey) {
850                        this.renameKey = renameKey;
851                        return self();
852                }
853
854                /**
855                 * Removes the prefix from a key before it accesses the underlying properties.
856                 * @param prefix to be removed from start of key.
857                 * @return this.
858                 */
859                public T removeKeyPrefix(String prefix) {
860                        return renameKey(k -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(k, prefix));
861                }
862
863        }

865        /**
866         * Builder for properties.
867         */
868        public final static class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
869
870                private @Nullable Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider = null;
871
872                private Builder() {
873                }
874
875                @Override
876                protected Builder self() {
877                        return this;
878                }
879
880                private Builder provider(Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider) {
881                        if (this.provider != null) {
882                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("from already set");
883                        }
884                        this.provider = provider;
885                        return this;
886                }
887
888                /**
889                 * Sets what is called on {@link LogProperties#valueOrNull(String)}.
890                 * @param function valueOrNull func.
891                 * @return this.
892                 */
893                public Builder fromFunction(@SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, @Nullable String> function) {
894                        return provider((b) -> new DefaultLogProperties(function,
895                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "function"), renameKey, order));
896                }
897
898                /**
899                 * Parses a string as {@link Properties}.
900                 * <p>
901                 * The parameter is the <strong>contents</strong> of a properties file, not a
902                 * resource, path, or file name. Passing a name such as
903                 * {@code "logging.properties"} does not load that file; it is parsed as a single
904                 * key with an empty value.
905                 * @param properties properties content as a string, for example
906                 * {@code "logging.level=INFO"}.
907                 * @return this.
908                 * @apiNote Rainbow Gum core does not read resources from the filesystem or the
909                 * classpath. If external properties are needed, it is the caller's responsibility
910                 * to read them into a string (or use a module that does, like
911                 * {@code rainbowgum-simple-props}).
912                 */
913                public Builder fromProperties(String properties) {
914                        if (description == null) {
915                                description = "PROPERTIES_STRING";
916                        }
917                        return fromFunction(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties)::get);
918                }
919
920                /**
921                 * Parses a string as a URI query string. If the URI has no query portion then it
922                 * will be equivalent to empty properties.
923                 * @param uri percent encoded uri with separator as "<code>&amp;</code>" and key
924                 * value separator of "<code>=</code>".
925                 * @return this.
926                 */
927                public Builder fromURIQuery(URI uri) {
928                        String query = uri.getRawQuery();
929                        return provider((b) -> queryToProperties(query,
930                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "URI_QUERY(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")")));
931                }
932
933                private MultiMapProperties queryToProperties(@Nullable String query, String description) {
934                        Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
935                        if (query == null) {
936                                multiMap = Map.of();
937                        }
938                        else {
939                                multiMap = parseMultiMap(query);
940                        }
941                        var properties = new MultiMapProperties(multiMap, description, renameKey, order);
942                        return properties;
943                }
944
945                /**
946                 * Builds LogProperties based on builder config.
947                 * @return this.
948                 */
949                public LogProperties build() {
950                        var f = this.provider;
951                        if (f == null) {
952                                if (!fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
953                                        return LogProperties.of(fallbacks);
954                                }
955                                throw new IllegalStateException("from was not set");
956                        }
957
958                        var first = f.apply(this);
959                        if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
960                                return first;
961                        }
962                        List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
963                        combined.add(first);
964                        combined.addAll(fallbacks);
965                        return LogProperties.of(combined);
966                }
967
968                static abstract class AbstractLogProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
969
970                        protected final String description;
971
972                        protected final Function<String, String> renameKey;
973
974                        protected final int order;
975
976                        public AbstractLogProperties(String description, Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
977                                super();
978                                this.description = description;
979                                this.renameKey = renameKey;
980                                this.order = order;
981                        }
982
983                        @Override
984                        public int order() {
985                                return this.order;
986                        }
987
988                        @Override
989                        public String description(String key) {
990                                String rename = renameKey.apply(key);
991                                return descriptionForKey(description, rename);
992                        }
993
994                        @Override
995                        public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
996                                out.append(description);
997                        }
998
999                        @Override
1000                        public String toString() {
1001                                return getClass().getSimpleName() + "[description='" + description + "', " + "order=" + order + "]";
1002                        }
1003
1004                }

1008                        private final Function<String, @Nullable String> func;

1012                                super(description, renameKey, order);

1025        /**
1026         * Properties that can list the keys they hold, so that with
1027         * {@link LogConfig.DebugModeType#HELP} (or {@link LogConfig.DebugModeType#ALL}) keys
1028         * that were set but never read can be reported. A source that renames keys should
1029         * name a key the way it is set in the source in {@link #description(String)}, since
1030         * that is how a suggested key is reported.
1031         */
1032        public interface Listable extends LogProperties {
1033
1034                /**
1035                 * The keys this source holds, as they are read (not renamed).
1036                 * @return keys.
1037                 */

1039

1042        /**
1043         * A base for properties read from a tree of nodes, such as a TOML, HOCON or YAML
1044         * document, or a configuration system that holds its settings as a tree. A subclass
1045         * says how to get a named member of a node and a node's value, and this class finds
1046         * the node for a key.
1047         * <p>
1048         * This class is only a way to implement {@link LogProperties}. Code that reads
1049         * properties should depend on {@link LogProperties}, not on this class.
1050         * <p>
1051         * A key is split on {@value LogProperties#SEP} into member names, except that a key
1052         * ending with a logger name, such as <code>logging.level.com.example</code>, ends
1053         * with one member: the logger name, which can contain dots or any other character.
1054         * The logger name is looked up as a single member of the node at the rest of the key
1055         * (<code>logging.level</code>) and, if there is no such member, split on
1056         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} like the rest of the key. The level, route level, change
1057         * and caller properties end with a logger name. For example in TOML:
1058         * {@snippet lang = toml :
1059         * [logging.level]
1060         * root = "warn"
1061         * "com.example" = "debug"
1062         * "com.example.sub" = "error"
1063         * }
1064         * The logger name <code>root</code> is the root logger, so a format that cannot have
1065         * a value at <code>logging.level</code> when it has members can set the root logger's
1066         * level as above.
1067         * <p>
1068         * {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} is called once for each lookup and nodes are not kept
1069         * between lookups, so a source whose tree changes at runtime can return its current
1070         * tree. Such a source should call {@link LogConfig.ChangePublisher#publish()} after a
1071         * change.
1072         * <p>
1073         * Methods added to this class in later versions will have names starting with
1074         * <code>do</code>, so a subclass should not declare methods with that prefix.
1075         *
1076         * @param <N> node type.
1077         */
1078        public static abstract class AbstractNested<N> implements LogProperties {
1079
1080                /**
1081                 * For subclasses.
1082                 */
1083                protected AbstractNested() {
1084                }
1085
1086                /**
1087                 * The top node of the tree, called once for each lookup.
1088                 * @return top node or <code>null</code> if there is none.
1089                 */
1090                protected abstract @Nullable N doRootNodeOrNull();
1091
1092                /**
1093                 * A member of a node.
1094                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or this method.
1095                 * @param name member name, which is not empty and may contain
1096                 * {@value LogProperties#SEP}.
1097                 * @return member or <code>null</code> if the node has no member with that name.
1098                 */
1099                protected abstract @Nullable N doMemberNodeOrNull(N node, String name);
1100
1101                /**
1102                 * The value of a node.
1103                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1104                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1105                 * @return value or <code>null</code> if the node has none, for example a node
1106                 * that only has members.
1107                 */
1108                protected abstract @Nullable String doValueNodeOrNull(N node);
1109
1110                /**
1111                 * The value of a node as a list, for a format that has lists. By default
1112                 * <code>null</code>, so {@link #listOrNull(String)} parses
1113                 * {@link #doValueNodeOrNull(Object)}.
1114                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1115                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1116                 * @return list or <code>null</code> if the node is not a list.
1117                 */
1118                protected @Nullable List<String> doListNodeOrNull(N node) {
1119                        return null;
1120                }
1121
1122                /**
1123                 * The value of a node as a map, for a format that has tables of values. By
1124                 * default <code>null</code>, so {@link #mapOrNull(String)} parses
1125                 * {@link #doValueNodeOrNull(Object)} or reads the map's keys from
1126                 * <code>key.keys</code>.
1127                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1128                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1129                 * @return map, iterating in a stable order, or <code>null</code> if the node is
1130                 * not a table of values.
1131                 */
1132                protected @Nullable Map<String, String> doMapNodeOrNull(N node) {
1133                        return null;
1134                }
1135
1136                @Override
1137                public final @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1138                        N node = node(key);
1139                        return node == null ? null : doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1140                }
1141
1142                @Override
1143                public final @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1144                        N node = node(key);
1145                        if (node == null) {
1146                                return null;
1147                        }
1148                        var list = doListNodeOrNull(node);
1149                        if (list != null) {
1150                                return list;
1151                        }
1152                        String value = doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1153                        return value == null ? null : LogProperties.parseList(value);
1154                }
1155
1156                @Override
1157                public final @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1158                        N node = node(key);
1159                        if (node != null) {
1160                                var map = doMapNodeOrNull(node);
1161                                if (map != null) {
1162                                        return map;
1163                                }
1164                                String value = doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1165                                if (value != null) {
1166                                        return LogProperties.parseMap(value);
1167                                }
1168                        }
1169                        return PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
1170                }
1171
1172                private @Nullable N node(String key) {
1173                        N root = doRootNodeOrNull();
1174                        if (root == null) {
1175                                return null;
1176                        }
1177                        var loggerKey = Loggers.Key.parseOrNull(key);
1178                        if (loggerKey == null) {
1179                                return path(root, key);
1180                        }
1181                        N prefix = path(root, loggerKey.prefix());
1182                        String loggerName = loggerKey.loggerName();
1183                        if (prefix == null || loggerName.isEmpty()) {
1184                                return prefix;
1185                        }
1186                        N member = doMemberNodeOrNull(prefix, loggerName);
1187                        return member != null ? member : path(prefix, loggerName);
1188                }
1189
1190                private @Nullable N path(N node, String path) {
1191                        N n = node;
1192                        int start = 0;
1193                        while (true) {
1194                                int end = path.indexOf(SEP, start);
1195                                String name = end < 0 ? path.substring(start) : path.substring(start, end);
1196                                if (name.isEmpty()) {
1197                                        return null;
1198                                }
1199                                N m = doMemberNodeOrNull(n, name);
1200                                if (m == null || end < 0) {
1201                                        return m;
1202                                }
1203                                n = m;
1204                                start = end + SEP.length();
1205                        }
1206                }
1207
1208        }
1209
1210        /**
1211         * A log properties that can be mutated like a map.
1212         */
1213        public interface MutableLogProperties extends LogProperties {
1214
1215                /**
1216                 * Assigns key to a value.
1217                 * @param key key.
1218                 * @param value value if null will remove the key.
1219                 * @return this.
1220                 */
1221                MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value);
1222
1223                /**
1224                 * Builder for MutableLogProperties.
1225                 * @return builder.
1226                 */
1227                public static Builder builder() {
1228                        return new Builder();
1229                }
1230
1231                /**
1232                 * Mutable Log properties builder.
1233                 */
1234                public final class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
1235
1236                        private Map<String, String> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1237
1238                        private Builder() {
1239                        }
1240
1241                        @Override
1242                        protected Builder self() {
1243                                return this;
1244                        }
1245
1246                        /**
1247                         * Sets the backing mutable map.
1248                         * @param map backing map.
1249                         * @return this.
1250                         */
1251                        public Builder with(Map<String, String> map) {
1252                                this.map = map;
1253                                return this;
1254                        }
1255
1256                        /**
1257                         * Parses a string as {@link Properties} useful for unit testing with Java
1258                         * multiline string literal.
1259                         * @param properties properties as a string.
1260                         * @return this.
1261                         */
1262                        public Builder copyProperties(String properties) {
1263                                map.putAll(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties));
1264                                return this;
1265                        }
1266
1267                        /**
1268                         * Builds a mutable log properties.
1269                         * @return mutable log properties.
1270                         */
1271                        public MutableLogProperties build() {
1272                                String description = this.description;
1273                                if (description == null) {
1274                                        description = "custom mutable";
1275                                }
1276                                var first = new MapLogProperties(map, description, renameKey, order);
1277                                if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
1278                                        return first;
1279                                }
1280                                List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
1281                                combined.add(first);
1282                                combined.addAll(fallbacks);
1283                                return new CompositeMutableLogProperties(sort(combined));
1284                        }
1285
1286                        private static final class MapLogProperties extends LogProperties.Builder.AbstractLogProperties
1287                                        implements MutableLogProperties {
1288
1289                                private final Map<String, String> map;
1290
1291                                MapLogProperties(Map<String, String> map, String description, Function<String, String> renameKey,
1292                                                int order) {
1293                                        super(description, renameKey, order);
1294                                        this.map = map;
1295                                }
1296
1297                                @Override
1298                                public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1299                                        return map.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1300                                }
1301
1302                                @Override
1303                                public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
1304                                        Objects.requireNonNull(key);
1305                                        key = renameKey.apply(key);
1306                                        if (value == null) {
1307                                                map.remove(key);
1308                                                return this;
1309                                        }
1310                                        map.put(key, value);
1311                                        return this;
1312                                }
1313
1314                        }
1315
1316                }
1317
1318        }

1320        /**
1321         * LogProperties builder.

1323         */
1324        public static Builder builder() {
1325                return new Builder();

1328        /**
1329         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1330         * use system properties. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and is
1331         * preferred that you get the properties through a config instance instead.</strong>
1332         * @return currently bound properties or system properties.
1333         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1334         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1335         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1336         */
1337        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties() {
1338                return findGlobalProperties(() -> StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
1339        }
1340
1341        /**
1342         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1343         * use the supplier as the fallback. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and
1344         * is preferred that you get the properties through a config instance
1345         * instead.</strong>
1346         * @param fallback supplier to use if no rainbow gum is bound.
1347         * @return currently bound properties or fallback.
1348         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1349         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1350         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1351         */
1352        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties(Supplier<? extends LogProperties> fallback) {
1353                var gum = RainbowGum.getOrNull();
1354                if (gum != null) {
1355                        return gum.config().properties();
1356                }
1357                return Objects.requireNonNull(fallback.get());
1358        }

1360        /**
1361         * Creates log properties from many log properties. Equal properties are only included
1362         * once.
1363         * @param logProperties list of properties.
1364         * @param fallback if the logProperties list is empty.
1365         * @return log properties
1366         */
1367        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties, LogProperties fallback) {
1368                if (logProperties.isEmpty()) {
1369                        return fallback;
1370                }
1371                if (logProperties.size() == 1) {
1372                        return Objects.requireNonNull(logProperties.get(0));
1373                }
1374                var array = sort(logProperties);
1375                return new CompositeLogProperties(array);
1376        }
1377
1378        private static LogProperties[] sort(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1379                @SuppressWarnings("null") // TODO eclipse array issue
1380                LogProperties[] array = logProperties.stream()
1381                        .filter(p -> p != StandardProperties.EMPTY)
1382                        // The same source listed twice adds nothing but noise in reports and errors.
1383                        .distinct()
1384                        .toArray(size -> new LogProperties[size]);
1385                Arrays.sort(array, Comparator.comparingInt(LogProperties::order).reversed());
1386                return array;
1387        }

1390         * Creates log properties from many log properties.
1391         * @param logProperties the list of properties.
1392         * @return if the logProperties is empty {@link StandardProperties#EMPTY} will be
1393         * used.
1394         */
1395        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1396                return of(logProperties, StandardProperties.EMPTY);
1397        }
