1399        /**
1400         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1401         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1402         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1403         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1404         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1405         * properties.
1406         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1407         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1408         * parameters.
1409         */
1410        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties) {
1411                return of(uri, prefix, properties, null);
1412        }
1413
1414        /**
1415         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1416         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1417         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1418         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1419         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1420         * properties.
1421         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1422         * @param uriKey where the URI came from.
1423         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1424         * parameters.
1425         */
1426        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties, @Nullable String uriKey) {
1427                /*
1428                 * TODO this should be integrated with the whole providers and registries.
1429                 */
1430                String propDesc = uriKey != null ? "[" + uriKey + "]->" : "";
1431                String description = propDesc + "URI(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")";
1432                var uriProperties = LogProperties.builder()
1433                        .description(description)
1434                        .fromURIQuery(uri)
1435                        .renameKey(s -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(s, prefix))
1436                        .build();
1437                var check = UnusedKeyCheck.findOrNull(properties);
1438                if (check != null) {
1439                        check.addUriQuery(uri, prefix, uriProperties);
1440                        /*
1441                         * Map members such as ?headers.x=y are read inside the query layer, so it is
1442                         * recorded like the config's own layers.
1443                         */
1444                        uriProperties = check.wrap(uriProperties);
1445                }
1446                var queryKeys = new LinkedHashSet<String>();
1447                String query = uri.getRawQuery();
1448                if (query != null) {
1449                        parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> queryKeys.add(prefix + k));
1450                }
1451                return LogProperties.of(List.of(properties, new UriQueryProperties(uriProperties, uriKey, queryKeys)));
1452        }
1453
1454        /**
1455         * Parse a {@linkplain URI#getRawQuery() URI query} in <a href=
1456         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1457         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded </a> format useful for parsing properties values
1458         * that have key values embedded in them. <strong>This parser unlike form encoding
1459         * uses <code>%20</code> for space as the data is coming from a URI.</strong>
1460         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1461         * @param consumer accept will be called for each entry and if key (left hand) does
1462         * not have a "<code>=</code>" following it the second parameter on the consumer
1463         * accept will be passed <code>null</code>.
1464         */
1465        public static void parseUriQuery(String query,
1466                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1467                parseUriQuery(query, true, consumer);
1468        }
1469
1470        /**
1471         * Parses a URI query formatted string to a Map.
1472         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1473         * @return decoded key values with last key winning over previous equal keys.
1474         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1475         */
1476        public static Map<String, String> parseMap(String query) {
1477                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1478                parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> {
1479                        if (v != null) {
1480                                m.put(k, v);
1481                        }
1482                });
1483                return m;
1484        }
1485
1486        /**
1487         * Parses a URI query for a multiple value map. The list values of the map maybe empty
1488         * if the query parameter does not have any values associated with it which would be
1489         * the case if there is a parameter (key) with no "<code>=</code>" following it. For
1490         * example the following would have three entries of <code>a,b,c</code> all with empty
1491         * list: <pre>
1492         * <code>
1493         * a&amp;b&amp;c&amp;
1494         * </code> </pre>
1495         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1496         * @return decoded key values with multiple keys grouped together in order found.
1497         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1498         */
1499        public static Map<String, List<String>> parseMultiMap(String query) {
1500                Map<String, List<String>> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1501                BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> f = (k, v) -> {
1502                        List<String> list = Objects.requireNonNull(m.computeIfAbsent(k, _k -> new ArrayList<String>()));
1503                        if (v != null) {
1504                                list.add(v);
1505                        }
1506                };
1507                parseUriQuery(query, f);
1508                return m;
1509        }
1510
1511        /**
1512         * Parses a list of strings from a string that is <a href=
1513         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1514         * percent encoded for escaping (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)</a> where the
1515         * separator can be either "<code>&amp;</code>" or "<code>,</code>".
1516         * <p>
1517         * An example would be using ampersand: <pre><code>
1518         *  "a&amp;b%20B&amp;c" -> ["a","b B","c"]
1519         *  </code> </pre> and comma: <pre><code>
1520         *  "a,b,c" -> ["a","b","c"]
1521         *  </code> </pre>
1522         * <p>
1523         * An element may be empty. One empty element at the start and one at the end are
1524         * dropped, so a value assembled from parts that may be missing still works
1525         * (<code>"a,"</code> and <code>",a,"</code> are <code>["a"]</code>), while every
1526         * other empty element is kept: <pre><code>
1527         *  "" -> []
1528         *  ",," -> [""]
1529         *  "a,,b" -> ["a","","b"]
1530         *  "a,," -> ["a",""]
1531         *  </code> </pre> An equals sign is part of the element: <code>"a=b"</code> is
1532         * <code>["a=b"]</code>.
1533         * @param query the comma or ampersand delimited string.
1534         * @return list of strings
1535         */
1536        public static List<String> parseList(String query) {
1537                List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();
1538                int start = 0;
1539                for (int i = 0; i < query.length(); i++) {
1540                        char c = query.charAt(i);
1541                        if (c == ',' || c == '&') {
1542                                list.add(query.substring(start, i));
1543                                start = i + 1;
1544                        }
1545                }
1546                list.add(query.substring(start));
1547                if (list.get(0).isEmpty()) {
1548                        list.remove(0);
1549                }
1550                if (!list.isEmpty() && list.get(list.size() - 1).isEmpty()) {
1551                        list.remove(list.size() - 1);
1552                }
1553                list.replaceAll(e -> PercentCodec.decode(e, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
1554                return list;
1555        }
1556
1557        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1558                parseUriQuery(query, decode, "[&,]", consumer);
1559        }
1560
1561        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, String sep,
1562                        BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1563                /*
1564                 * TODO default java split has issues but is very fast
1565                 */
1566                @SuppressWarnings("StringSplitter")
1567                String[] pairs = query.split(sep);
1568                for (String pair : pairs) {
1569                        int idx = pair.indexOf("=");
1570                        String key;
1571                        String value;
1572                        if (idx == 0) {
1573                                continue;
1574                        }
1575                        else if (idx < 0) {
1576                                key = pair;
1577                                value = null;
1578                        }
1579                        else {
1580                                key = pair.substring(0, idx);
1581                                value = pair.substring(idx + 1);
1582                        }
1583                        if (decode) {
1584                                key = PercentCodec.decode(key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1585                                if (value != null) {
1586                                        value = PercentCodec.decode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1587                                }
1588
1589                        }
1590                        if (key.isBlank()) {
1591                                continue;
1592                        }
1593                        consumer.accept(key, value);
1594                }
1595        }
1596
1597        /**
1598         * Common static log properties such as System properties ane environment variables.
1599         */
1600        @CaseChanging
1601        enum StandardProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1602
1603                /**
1604                 * Empty properties. The order is <code>-1</code>.
1605                 */
1606                EMPTY {
1607                        @Override
1608                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1609                                return null;
1610                        }
1611
1612                        @Override
1613                        public int order() {
1614                                return -1;
1615                        }
1616                },
1617                /**
1618                 * Uses {@link System#getProperty(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}. The
1619                 * {@link #order()} is <code>400</code> which the same value as MicroProfile
1620                 * config ordinal.
1621                 */
1622                SYSTEM_PROPERTIES {
1623                        @Override
1624                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1625                                return System.getProperty(key);
1626                        }
1627
1628                        @Override
1629                        public int order() {
1630                                return 400;
1631                        }
1632                },
1633                /**
1634                 * Uses {@link System#getenv(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}.The
1635                 * {@link #order()} is <code>300</code> which is the same value as MicroProfile
1636                 * config ordinal.
1637                 */
1638                ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES {
1639                        @Override
1640                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1641                                return System.getenv(translateKey(key));
1642                        }
1643
1644                        @Override
1645                        protected String translateKey(String key) {
1646                                return key.replace(".", "_");
1647                        }
1648
1649                        @Override
1650                        public int order() {
1651                                return 300;
1652                        }
1653                };
1654
1655                @Override
1656                public String description(String key) {
1657                        String k = translateKey(key);
1658                        return name() + "[" + k + "]";
1659                }
1660
1661                /*
1662                 * Each constant's own per-constant class body (see EMPTY/SYSTEM_PROPERTIES/
1663                 * ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES above) makes getClass() an anonymous subclass with no
1664                 * canonical name, so without this LogPropertiesReporting's fallback chain would
1665                 * land on the description(dummyKey) branch instead: name() alone is a cleaner
1666                 * report for the single most common LogProperties in practice (the default when
1667                 * nothing else is configured).
1668                 */
1669                @Override
1670                public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1671                        out.append(name());
1672                }
1673
1674                /**
1675                 * Translate the key.
1676                 * @param key input
1677                 * @return output
1678                 */
1679                protected String translateKey(String key) {
1680                        return key;
1681                }
1682
1683        }
1684
1685        /**
1686         * Searches a {@value LogProperties#SEP} separated property path recursing up the path
1687         * till a non null value (not missing) is found.
1688         * <p>
1689         * For example assume we have a single property set like
1690         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff=DEBUG</code> and we call this function with
1691         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code>.
1692         * <ol>
1693         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1694         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1695         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff</code> will resolve to <code>"DEBUG"</code>, stop
1696         * and return <code>"DEBUG"</code>.</li>
1697         * </ol>
1698         * @param <T> type to return.
1699         * @param key the initial path.
1700         * @param resolveFunc function that returns the value at path or <code>null</code>.
1701         * @return value or <code>null</code> if no non null value can be found.
1702         */
1703        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
1704        public static <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findUpPathOrNull(String key,
1705                        Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc) {
1706                return searchPath(key, resolveFunc, SEP);
1707        }
1708
1709        private static <T> @Nullable T searchPath(String key, Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc, String sep) {
1710                String tempName = key;
1711                @Nullable T level = null;
1712                int indexOfLastDot = tempName.length();
1713                while ((level == null) && (indexOfLastDot > -1)) {
1714                        tempName = tempName.substring(0, indexOfLastDot);
1715                        level = resolveFunc.apply(tempName);
1716                        indexOfLastDot = tempName.lastIndexOf(sep);
1717                }
1718                if (level != null) {
1719                        return level;
1720                }
1721                return resolveFunc.apply("");
1722        }
1723
1724        /**
1725         * Concats a key using {@link #SEP} to the root prefix.
1726         * @param name key.
1727         * @return concat key.
1728         */
1729        static String concatKey(String name) {
1730                return concatKey(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX, name);
1731        }
1732
1733        /**
1734         * Concats a keys using {@link #SEP} as the separator.
1735         * @param prefix start of key.
1736         * @param name second part of key.
1737         * @return key.
1738         */
1739        static String concatKey(String prefix, String name) {
1740                if (name.equals("")) {
1741                        return prefix;
1742                }
1743                if (prefix.equals("")) {
1744                        return name;
1745                }
1746                if (prefix.endsWith(".")) {
1747                        prefix = prefix.substring(0, prefix.length() - 1);
1748                }
1749                if (name.startsWith(SEP)) {
1750                        return prefix + name;
1751                }
1752                return prefix + SEP + name;
1753        }
1754
1755        /**
1756         * Replace "{name}" tokens in property names.
1757         * @param key property name.
1758         * @param parameters tokens to replace with entry values.
1759         * @return interpolated property key.
1760         * @see #interpolateKey(String, Function)
1761         */
1762        static String interpolateKey(String key, Map<String, String> parameters) {
1763                return interpolateKey(key, parameters::get);
1764        }
1765
1766        /**
1767         * Replaces property <strong>key</strong> parameters by using the lookup function.
1768         * Property keys are often parameterized usually by some name. The parameters are
1769         * surrounded by curly braces and replaced by the lookup function. An example of the
1770         * format is <code>a.{PARAM}</code> which has a parameter named <code>PARAM</code>. If
1771         * the lookup function has <code>PARAM->b</code> then the result will be
1772         * <code>a.b</code>. If a value for a parameter is null (indicates not found) an
1773         * exception is thrown.
1774         * @param key to be interpolated.
1775         * @param lookup function that may return null for a parameter.
1776         * @return interpolated key with all parameters replaced.
1777         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the lookup function does not have a value for a
1778         * parameter.
1779         */
1780        public static String interpolateKey(String key,
1781                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, ? extends @Nullable String> lookup)
1782                        throws IllegalArgumentException {
1783                var parameters = keyParameters(key);
1784                String result = key;
1785                for (String k : parameters) {
1786                        var v = lookup.apply(k);
1787                        if (v == null) {
1788                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
1789                                                "Keyed parameter missing. key: '" + key + "' parameter: '" + k + "'");
1790                        }
1791                        LogProperty.Validator.validateKeyParameterValue(key, k, v);
1792                        result = result.replace("{" + k + "}", v);
1793                }
1794                return result;
1795        }
1796
1797        /**
1798         * Interpolates a named key which is a property key that has a {@value #NAME}.
1799         * @param key with name parameters.
1800         * @param name replace name token.
1801         * @return interpolated property key.
1802         */
1803        static String interpolateNamedKey(String key, String name) {
1804                return interpolateKey(key, Map.of(NAME, name));
1805        }
1806
1807        /**
1808         * Remove key prefix from the key. Prefix should end in "." but this method does not
1809         * check that.
1810         * @param key key whose prefix will be removed.
1811         * @param prefix property name prefix.
1812         * @return prefix removed if the string is prefixed.
1813         */
1814        static String removeKeyPrefix(String key, String prefix) {
1815                if (key.startsWith(prefix)) {
1816                        return key.substring(prefix.length());
1817                }
1818                return key;
1819        }
1820
1821        /**
1822         * Property prefix parameter pattern.
1823         */
1824        static final Pattern PARAMETER_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("\\{(.*?)\\}");
1825
1826        /**
1827         * Extract key parameters with {@link #PARAMETER_PATTERN}.
1828         * @param key also known as property name.
1829         * @return parameters in key.
1830         */
1831        static Set<String> keyParameters(String key) {
1832                Set<String> tokens = new LinkedHashSet<>();
1833                Matcher matcher = PARAMETER_PATTERN.matcher(key);
1834                while (matcher.find()) {
1835                        var t = matcher.group(1);
1836                        if (t == null) {
1837                                throw new IllegalStateException("bug with parameter pattern regex.");
1838                        }
1839                        tokens.add(t);
1840                }
1841                return tokens;
1842        }
1843
1844        /**
1845         * Validate key parameters.
1846         * @param key key to be interpolated with parameters.
1847         * @param parameters names of parameters which must <strong>equal</strong> the set of
1848         * the found parameters. while the order obviously does not matter the set cannot have
1849         * more parameters than found in the key.
1850         */
1851        static void validateKeyParameters(String key, Set<String> parameters) {
1852                var keyParameters = keyParameters(key);
1853                if (!parameters.equals(keyParameters)) {
1854                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Keyed parameter mismatch. key: '" + key + "' , key parameters: "
1855                                        + keyParameters + " provided parameters: " + parameters);
1856                }
1857        }
1858
1859        /**
1860         * Standard way to produce description for a key.
1861         * @param type the properties type name.
1862         * @param key the properties key translated.
1863         * @return description for key.
1864         */
1865        static String descriptionForKey(String type, String key) {
1866                return type + "[" + key + "]";
1867        }
1868
1869        /**
1870         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1871         * similar), without a line number.
1872         * @param type the properties type name.
1873         * @param resource file like name.
1874         * @param key the properties key translated.
1875         * @return description for key.
1876         */
1877        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key) {
1878                return type + "[" + resource + "][" + key + "]";
1879        }
1880
1881        /**
1882         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1883         * similar) at a known index, usually a line number.
1884         * @param type the properties type name.
1885         * @param resource file like name.
1886         * @param key the properties key translated.
1887         * @param index usually line number of where key found.
1888         * @return description for key.
1889         */
1890        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key, long index) {
1891                return type + "[" + resource + ":" + index + "][" + key + "]";
1892        }
1893
1894}

1896final class MultiMapProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
1897
1898        private final Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
1899
1900        public MultiMapProperties(Map<String, List<String>> multiMap, String description,
1901                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
1902                super(description, renameKey, order);
1903                this.multiMap = multiMap;
1904        }
1905
1906        @Override
1907        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1908                return _valueOrNull(renameKey.apply(key));
1909        }
1910
1911        private @Nullable String _valueOrNull(String key) {
1912                var list = multiMap.get(key);
1913                if (list == null || list.isEmpty()) {
1914                        return null;
1915                }
1916                return list.get(0);
1917        }
1918
1919        @Override
1920        public @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1921                return multiMap.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1922        }
1923
1924        @Override
1925        public @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1926                String s = valueOrNull(key);
1927                if (s != null) {
1928                        return LogProperties.parseMap(s);
1929                }
1930                var map = PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
1931                if (map != null) {
1932                        return map;
1933                }
1934                /*
1935                 * Now we check for dotted notation since key was not set. key.subkey=value
1936                 */
1937                String prefix = renameKey.apply(key) + LogProperties.SEP;
1938                LinkedHashMap<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1939                for (var k : multiMap.keySet()) {
1940                        if (k.startsWith(prefix) && !k.equals(prefix)) {
1941                                String v = _valueOrNull(k);
1942                                if (v != null) {
1943                                        String _k = k.substring(prefix.length());
1944                                        m.put(_k, v);
1945                                }
1946                        }
1947                }
1948                return m.isEmpty() ? null : m;
1949        }
1950
1951}
1952
1953interface ListLogProperties extends LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1954
1955        @Override
1956        default @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1957                for (var props : properties()) {
1958                        var value = props.valueOrNull(key);
1959                        if (value != null) {
1960                                return value;
1961                        }
1962                }
1963                return null;
1964        }
1965
1966        @Override
1967        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
1968                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
1969                for (var props : properties()) {
1970                        var value = props.visit(key, visitor);
1971                        if (value != null) {
1972                                return value;
1973                        }
1974                }
1975                return null;
1976        }
1977
1978        @Override
1979        default String description(String key) {
1980                var descriptions = new ArrayList<String>();
1981                visit(key, (source, sourceKey) -> {
1982                        descriptions.add(source.description(sourceKey));
1983                        return null;
1984                });
1985                String description = String.join(", ", descriptions);
1986                if (description.length() > 120) {
1987                        return "\n    " + String.join(",\n    ", descriptions);
1988                }
1989                return description;
1990        }
1991
1992        LogProperties[] properties();
1993
1994        default StringBuilder toString(StringBuilder sb) {
1995                sb.append(getClass().getSimpleName());
1996                sb.append("[properties=").append(Arrays.deepToString(properties())).append("]");
1997                return sb;
1998        }
1999
2000        /*
2001         * Reports components separated by commas without the error description's line
2002         * wrapping (via LogPropertiesReporting.describe, the same fallback chain
2003         * LogReporter#appendGlobalProperties uses for the top level LogProperties a LogConfig
2004         * was built with) rather than per key.
2005         */
2006        @Override
2007        default void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
2008                boolean first = true;
2009                for (var p : properties()) {
2010                        if (first) {
2011                                first = false;
2012                        }
2013                        else {
2014                                out.append(", ");
2015                        }
2016                        LogPropertiesReporting.describe(out, p);
2017                }
2018        }
2019
2020}
2021
2022/*
2023 * Shared by ListLogProperties#report(Appendable) (recursively, per component) and
2024 * LogReporter's own appendGlobalProperties(Appendable, LogProperties) (for the top level
2025 * LogProperties a LogConfig was built with), so there is exactly one fallback chain for
2026 * "how do we describe an arbitrary LogProperties for a report": an explicit
2027 * Reportable#report(...) if implemented, else the concrete class' fully qualified name
2028 * (stable and free: no override needed), else, only for the rare case where the FQCN
2029 * itself is null (e.g. one of StandardProperties' own per constant enum bodies, which are
2030 * anonymous classes under the hood, before it implemented Reportable directly),
2031 * description(key) with a dummy key, since that is the only description() such a
2032 * LogProperties is guaranteed to answer at all.
2033 */
2034final class LogPropertiesReporting {
2035
2036        static final String DESCRIBE_KEY = "logging.reporter.describe";
2037
2038        private LogPropertiesReporting() {
2039        }
2040
2041        static void describe(Appendable out, LogProperties properties) throws IOException {
2042                if (properties instanceof LogReporter.Reportable r) {
2043                        r.report(out);
2044                        return;
2045                }
2046                String fqcn = properties.getClass().getCanonicalName();
2047                if (fqcn != null) {
2048                        out.append(fqcn);
2049                        return;
2050                }
2051                out.append(properties.description(DESCRIBE_KEY));
2052        }
2053
2054}

2056@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent") // TODO we did this originall because it was hot
2057                                                                                        // path but not anymore
2058record CompositeMutableLogProperties(LogProperties[] properties) implements ListLogProperties, MutableLogProperties {
2059
2060        @Override
2061        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // identity check to avoid self-recursion if a
2062                                                                                        // composite contains itself
2063        public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
2064                for (var p : properties()) {
2065                        if (p instanceof MutableLogProperties mp && mp != this) {
2066                                mp.put(key, value);
2067                                return this;
2068                        }
2069                }
2070                return this;
2071        }
2072
2073        @Override
2074        public String toString() {
2075                return toString(new StringBuilder()).toString();
2076        }
2077
2078}

2089final class PropertiesParser {
2090
2091        private PropertiesParser() {
2092        }
2093
2094        static Map<String, String> readProperties(String input) {
2095                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
2096                StringReader sr = new StringReader(input);
2097                try {
2098                        readProperties(sr, m::put);
2099                }
2100                catch (IOException e) {
2101                        throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
2102                }
2103                return m;
2104        }
2105
2106        static void readProperties(Reader reader, BiConsumer<String, String> consumer) throws IOException {
2107                Properties bp = prepareProperties(consumer);
2108                bp.load(reader);
2109        }
2110
2111        private static Properties prepareProperties(BiConsumer<String, String> consumer) {
2112                // Hack to use properties class to load but our map for preserved order
2113                @SuppressWarnings({ "serial", "nullness" })
2114                Properties bp = new Properties() {
2115                        @Override
2116                        @SuppressWarnings({ "nullness", "keyfor", "UnsynchronizedOverridesSynchronized" }) // checker
2117                                                                                                                                                                                                // bug
2118                        public @Nullable Object put(Object key, Object value) {
2119                                Objects.requireNonNull(key);
2120                                Objects.requireNonNull(value);
2121                                consumer.accept((String) key, (String) value);
2122                                return null;
2123                        }
2124                };
2125                return bp;
2126        }
2127
2128}
2129
2130/*
2131 * The key.keys form of LogProperties.mapOrNull, shared with implementations that override
2132 * it.
2133 */
2134final class PropertyMaps {
2135
2136        private PropertyMaps() {
2137        }
2138
2139        static @Nullable Map<String, String> fromKeys(LogProperties properties, String key) {
2140                String keysKey = key + LogProperties.SEP + LogProperties.MAP_KEYS_SUFFIX;
2141                List<String> keys = properties.listOrNull(keysKey);
2142                if (keys == null) {
2143                        return null;
2144                }
2145                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
2146                for (String k : keys) {
2147                        if (k.isEmpty()) {
2148                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("'" + keysKey + "' has an empty map key");
2149                        }
2150                        String valueKey = key + LogProperties.SEP + k;
2151                        String v = properties.valueOrNull(valueKey);
2152                        if (v == null) {
2153                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
2154                                                "map key '" + k + "' is listed in '" + keysKey + "' but '" + valueKey + "' is missing");
2155                        }
2156                        m.put(k, v);
2157                }
2158                return m;
2159        }
2160
2161}

2163/*
2164 * Marks the layer that holds a component URI's query parameters, so a sensitive property
2165 * can refuse a value from it.
2166 */
2167final class UriQueryProperties extends ForwardingLogProperties {
2168
2169        private final LogProperties delegate;
2170
2171        private final @Nullable String uriKey;
2172
2173        private final Set<String> keys;
2174
2175        UriQueryProperties(LogProperties delegate, @Nullable String uriKey, Set<String> keys) {
2176                this.delegate = delegate;
2177                this.uriKey = uriKey;
2178                this.keys = Set.copyOf(keys);
2179        }
2180
2181        /*
2182         * Whether a query parameter sets the key, including as a map member such as
2183         * ?headers.Authorization=x for headers.
2184         */
2185        boolean sets(String key) {
2186                for (String k : keys) {
2187                        if (k.equals(key) || k.startsWith(key + SEP)) {
2188                                return true;
2189                        }
2190                }
2191                return false;
2192        }
2193
2194        @Override
2195        protected LogProperties delegate() {
2196                return delegate;
2197        }
2198
2199        @Nullable String uriKey() {
2200                return uriKey;
2201        }
2202
2203        @Override
2204        public String toString() {
2205                return delegate.toString();
2206        }
2207
2208}
